title: Ground-State Phase Diagram of the Effective Model with Antiferromagnetic Nearest-Neighbor and Ferromagnetic Next-Nearest-Neighbor Interactions in 1/1 Periodic Approximants to Icosahedral Quasicrystals
abstract: By performing complete enumeration of all configurations of magnetic moments, we have determined the ground-state phase diagram of the effective model with antiferromagnetic nearest-neighbor interactions $J_1$ and ferromagnetic next-nearest-neighbor interactions $J_2$ on the 1/1 periodic approximant to icosahedral quasicrystal. Depending on the ratio of $J_2/J_1$ and the magnetic anisotropy arising from the crystalline electric field, various non-collinear ferrimagnetic orders and antiferromagnetic orders are shown to be stabilized, whose magnetic space groups are identified as $R\bar{3}$, $C2'/m'$, $Pm'm'2$ and $I_{\rm P}m'\bar{3}'$. We have revealed the topological as well as magnetic property of each ground state with degeneracy, which is useful to understand experimental observations of magnetic structures and domains in the rare-earth-based 1/1 approximants.
summary: This theoretical work maps the magnetic ground-state phase diagram for rare-earth magnetic systems modeled on icosahedral quasicrystal approximants. By analyzing the competition between antiferromagnetic and ferromagnetic interactions, the authors identify several stable non-collinear magnetic orders. The study is significant for linking crystal structure, magnetic interactions, and topological properties in complex materials.
main_problem: The study aims to determine the ground-state phase diagram of an effective magnetic model describing interactions in 1/1 periodic approximants to icosahedral quasicrystals.
main_result: The research reveals that various non-collinear ferrimagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders are stabilized, with the specific ground state depending critically on the ratio of $J_2/J_1$ and the magnetic anisotropy angle $	heta$.
method: The authors used complete enumeration of magnetic moment configurations combined with topological analysis (calculating total chirality $\chi_T$ and topological charge $n$) to map the phase diagram.
model_or_system: The system is based on rare-earth-based 1/1 approximants to icosahedral quasicrystals. The effective Hamiltonian includes nearest-neighbor (AFM, $J_1$) and next-nearest-neighbor (FM, $J_2$) interactions, alongside magnetic anisotropy from the Crystal Electric Field (CEF).
key_observables: Ground-state phase diagram, magnetic space groups ($ ar{R}3$, $C2'/m'$, etc.), topological charge ($n$), and total chirality ($\chi_T$).
important_parameters: The ratio $J_2/J_1$ and the magnetic anisotropy angle $	heta$ are the primary tuning parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the effective model Hamiltonian and the assumption that ground states can be found via complete enumeration of magnetic configurations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Tsai-type cluster components, the geometry of N.N. and N.N.N. bonds, the main phase diagram mapping stable magnetic structures vs. $J_2/J_1$ and $	heta$, and the $	heta$ dependence of magnetic moments and chirality.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the magnetic interactions (N.N. and N.N.N.) within the quasicrystal structure, calculates topological invariants, and maps out the resulting ground-state phase diagram based on interaction ratios and anisotropy.
why_interesting: The combination of geometric frustration (quasicrystals) with magnetic interactions and topological invariants provides a rich platform for understanding emergent quantum magnetic phenomena beyond simple lattice models.
